definition: Granular means broken down into fine detail.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word granular. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know granular should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The sleep app's granular log slices each night into five-minute bands of light, deep, and dreaming.
Broad sits at the opposite end from granular — one number for the month, and no way to see inside it.
Detailed stops short of granular — a detailed report covers many points; a granular one splits the data down to its smallest grains.

Fine-grained is the literal image granular also draws — detail carried down to the individual grain. The two are nearly twins; granular is the analyst's preferred word for data, budgets, and logs, promising that the information arrives already split into its smallest working units.

An itemized bill lists every charge on its own line so each entry can be checked. Granular goes past listing: it promises resolution, data milled into units so small that hidden patterns surface. Itemized is about accountability, line by line; granular is about how finely the whole is split.

Grandfather's orchard ledger gave one line to each season: good year, fair year, hard frost.
His grandson keeps the same ledger on a laptop, and his granular records run to forty columns — yield by row, by rootstock, by picking day, even by which crew carried the sacks.
When blight crept in, the old book could only have said a bad year; the new one showed it starting in row nine, a fortnight before anyone saw a spot.
Granular is the exact word for the grandson's records, because granular means broken down into fine detail — the harvest ground down to its grains.
Detailed praises thoroughness loosely; granular names the structure itself: information split into units so small that patterns show up long before they reach the surface.
Granular is the analyst's adjective — data, budgets, logs — and it promises structure, not just abundance: the information comes pre-milled into small units.
Detailed is the loose everyday cousin; fine-grained the literal twin.
Its opposite number in this unit is aggregate: aggregate rolls everything up into one figure, granular grinds the figure back down into grains.

For years the city's road report was a single sentence: 'Conditions remain acceptable.' The new public dashboard is granular instead.
It logs every pothole complaint by street, by lane, and by hour, and it lets anyone slice the record down to a single block.
The difference showed within a month.
Viewed block by block, the data revealed that one neighborhood generated a third of all complaints, most of them along two bus routes.
A summary number had hidden that pattern for a decade; no one could see inside it.
Now the paving crews plan their week from the dashboard's smallest units, and the complaints line, for the first time anyone can remember, is falling.
